🧠 Crypto News Brief: Washington blinked and crypto flinched. The SEC's abrupt cancellation of its Regulation Crypto vote knocked the wind out of the tokenization trade, while a second straight day of ETF redemptions dragged bitcoin back under $63,000. Institutional builders kept building anyway. 🏛️ SEC Cancels Its First Major Crypto Rulemaking Vote The Securities and Exchange Commission abruptly scrapped the Friday open meeting at which commissioners were set to propose "Regulation Crypto" — the agency's first formal crypto rulemaking and the centerpiece of Chair Paul Atkins' agenda. The regulator cited an unforeseen scheduling issue and offered no replacement date, leaving a roughly 400-page proposal that would have created tailored offering exemptions for token issuers stranded in limbo alongside the stalled CLARITY Act. Read full story 📉 Tokenization Stocks Slide on the Regulatory Setback Bullish, Coinbase and Circle all closed lower Friday as investors marked down the near-term odds for crypto's Wall Street push. The SEC also pushed back its long-awaited "innovation exemption" covering tokenized securities trading, and analysts warned that the combination of an indefinite rulemaking delay and unresolved questions over the agency's legal authority could stretch out the adoption curve for real-world asset tokenization. More details ₿ Bitcoin Slips Under $63,000 as ETFs Post a Two-Day Drawdown Bitcoin fell to its lowest level since August 3, wiping out the whole of the previous week's rally, after spot ETFs bled roughly $192 million across back-to-back sessions — the first such stretch since late July. Cooler-than-expected U.S. producer price data lifted equities but did nothing for crypto, and derivatives desks reported growing bearish positioning even as implied volatility drifted toward 2026 lows. Read more ⚔️ Strategy Fires Back at MSCI Over Index Exclusion Threat Michael Saylor's Strategy publicly rejected MSCI's proposed "non-operating company" screen, telling the index provider it should measure markets rather than decide which assets public companies may own. The five-ratio test would delete Strategy, Metaplanet and uranium holder Yellow Cake from the ACWI IMI at the November review; JPMorgan has previously pegged the resulting forced passive selling in MSTR at around $2.8 billion.
